newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mostly steady on Friday as dealers monitored the sharp drop in Chicago Board of Trade corn, soybean and soymeal prices.
"Nobody is a buyer," one Buffalo dealer said.

He also noted that the Midwestern markets appeared to be under pressure. But in the U.S. northeast, the millfeed market was very thin with just enough flour mill run time to take care of nearby demand.
Buffalo millfeed prices were bid at $85 a short ton and offered at $89, down $3 from Thursday.
"But the (reduced) run times are keeping prices higher than what they normally would be -- $89 is a good price compared to other markets," he said.
"We need a little bit extra run time here if there is any pressure to come to our pricing," he added.
Other dealers said activity was quiet.
In the southeast, dealers said warmer temperatures have spurred pasture growth, lessening the demand for feed.
